BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. It also includes a **"Reviewer Efficiency Note"** asking us to treat clauses marked [STANDARD] as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to proceed as if we have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." We should reject that note entirely:

- The note comes from the counterparty, and we have no record of agreeing to any of it. Playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3 says a label like "standard," "agreed" or "cleared" in a counterparty document does not make it so.
- Nearly every [STANDARD] item is a material departure from our positions. The labels sit on the clauses that most need scrutiny.
- **Recommendation:** Reply in writing that no clause is agreed, that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labels and the efficiency note are not accepted, and that all positions remain open pending our mark-up.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also contradicts several statements in its Update. On Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses and the incident, the disclosed facts weaken the Seller's position. We should use that.

**Freshness point:** The disclosures speak as at **22 September 2026**, about six weeks ago. Before relying on any of them, we should request bring-down confirmation of Bluefen, Riverlark payout, the DD-006 investigation, Ironquay payment status and the bonus position.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General liability cap (cl 12.1): Seller proposes 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft. **No such authority has been given.**
- The Seller's figure matching our fallback does not make it acceptable. That match is exactly the trap the playbook warns about. Even with authority, the fallback would not be acceptable alongside the Seller's thresholds, time limits and carve-out removals, which compound the reduction.
- **Push back:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not mention or concede the fallback without Amelia's written authority.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k, basket AUD 250k, excess-only
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- The Seller's de minimis is 5x ours and its basket is 5x ours. The "excess only" (deductible) structure permanently removes AUD 250k of recovery. Together these would wipe out most mid-sized claims.
- **Push back:** AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping (first-dollar) basis.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months, plus a blanket "applies to all Claims" rule
- **Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- The second sentence is more dangerous than the first. "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a **hidden general-regime override**. It would pull title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general caps and time limits by default.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the sweep-up sentence. State expressly that general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment or covenant claims.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties: Seller proposes the same caps and time limits as general warranties
- **Playbook:** a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and exclusion from the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title fails, the buyer has not acquired what it paid for. Capping recovery at 20% of price would leave us bearing about 80% of the loss on a failed title.
- **Push back:** reinstate a separate Fundamental regime in full.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): "apply to all Claims of any nature"
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **No one may waive this.**
- As drafted, the provisions would arguably extend to fraud claims. This is a non-negotiable point, and we have no fallback.
- **Push back:** insert an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, by the Seller or its officers, employees or advisers, from every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and the non-reliance clause. Also carve Fundamental, Tax, IP and specific-indemnity claims out of the general limitations.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2): whole-data-room and public-register disclosure
- **Playbook:** require specific fair disclosure. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room. DL 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." Taken together, nearly any warranty could be neutralised by something buried in the data room.
- DL 1.4 (no admission of breach, liability or requirement) is broadly acceptable in principle. However, it must not dilute the effect of specific disclosures against the warranties.
- **Push back:** delete DL 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should be limited to matters fairly disclosed in the specific paragraphs of the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, and cross-referenced to the relevant warranty. The Seller has represented that the general disclosure is "without limiting any specific disclosure," so it cannot say the specific disclosures are inadequate.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): blanket exclusion, including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- This clause is worse than an actual-knowledge bar. It imputes constructive knowledge to us and our advisers, which would make our own due diligence a defence for the Seller. It would also defeat the specific indemnities, which exist precisely because we know about the issues.
- **Push back:** delete cl 8.3. Separately, make any Seller "awareness" qualifiers on warranties refer to named individuals' actual knowledge after reasonable enquiry. Those individuals should be identified from the Seller's management; the playbook does not name them, so we should propose names.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller says:** "addressed," with reasonable endeavours and consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the written consent.
- **The Seller's own DL para 2 says:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m). Clause 11.2 requires change-of-control consent, and clause 11.3 attaches conditions. **No final consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied has been provided.** The matter is therefore not "addressed."
- **Playbook:** effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied, before Completion. Consent-on-delivery is not enough. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.
- Under consent-on-delivery, a conditional consent whose 11.3 conditions are unmet could satisfy the Condition. We could then complete and lose 30% of revenue.
- **Push back:** a Condition Precedent requiring an unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, in form and substance satisfactory to the Buyer, plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met, delivered before Completion. Pair this with a stronger Seller obligation, such as all reasonable endeavours plus specified steps, and a Buyer-only right to waive.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller says:** release "to be provided following Completion."
- **DL para 3:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding. Change-of-control at 8.1, discharge at 9.2. **Not repaid, and no discharge provided.**
- **Playbook:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable lender undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval.
- On a debt-free basis, a post-Completion release leaves us acquiring a company with live security and a possible change-of-control default under 8.1. We would be relying on the Seller's goodwill to clear it.
- **Push back:** a Completion deliverable of a Riverlark payout letter dated close to Completion, payment directly from the funds flow, and executed releases and discharges (including PPSR) delivered at Completion. The amount must be deducted as Debt. We should not discuss any post-Completion route without Amelia's approval and a lender's irrevocable undertaking.

### 10. Employee bonuses (funds flow / DD-005)
- **Seller says:** the AUD 420k bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. **DL para 5 confirms** they are absent from the funds flow and does not address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or be seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- The bonuses are Company liabilities triggered by Completion. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company, and therefore we, would bear them, plus on-costs.
- **Push back:** either deduct them as Debt or a transaction cost, with on-costs, as an express line item paid through payroll at Completion, or obtain a Seller-funded mechanism backed by a specific indemnity covering the amounts and all on-costs. The on-cost amount must be quantified; it has not been.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Seller says:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate."
- **DL para 4:** transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, which is unverified. There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- A payment-only indemnity does not address the real risk, which is that the Company does not own IP it uses. That exposes us to infringement claims, loss of use, re-development cost and third-party claims, none of which are capped at the outstanding fee.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to or right to use the Ironquay deliverables, including infringement claims.
  - Keep the cure route: payment of outstanding SOW3 fees at or before Completion, verified by a bank/remittance record and Ironquay's written confirmation, plus a confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable.
  - Exclude the indemnity from the general limitations.
  - Do not treat AUD 180k as the confirmed figure in either direction.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6, DD-006)
- **Seller says:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **DL para 6:** a download link was sent to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records may be affected (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). Access, scope and notification obligation are not established, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- We should not accept the Seller's "not expected to be material" characterisation, because the investigation has not concluded. We also should not overstate the matter or assert a notifiable breach or a loss figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete a proper investigation (independent if appropriate), give regular written updates and the final findings to the Buyer, and consult the Buyer before any notification or regulator/customer communication.
  - Strike "not expected to be material" from any warranty or disclosure language.
  - Seek a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, outside the general limitations.
  - Request a current status update, since the latest disclosure is from 22 September.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011, AUD 330k)
- **Seller says:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **DL para 8:** three related renewals of AUD 110k each, to be read together for timing and scope. The DL does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** assess them, with no automatic Debt classification and no price deduction.
- The Seller has asserted "ordinary course" without support, and its own disclosure does not establish it. We should not concede the characterisation, but our playbook does not support demanding a deduction either.
- **Action:** request the contracts, timing, termination rights, accrual status and business rationale. Ask whether the three renewals were split, related or accelerated before Completion. Reserve the position on treatment, such as Debt, working capital, indemnity or an ordinary-course covenant, until the facts are assessed.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties
- **Seller says:** "settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- They are not settled. Placing them in the general regime with a 20% cap and 18 months would be the hidden override flagged in item 3.
- **Response:** state that Tax and IP remain open and are to be negotiated as separate categories. Do not assert unlimited liability as a position either.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Seller says:** title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. **DL para 10** itself acknowledges that this is only the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Playbook:** require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Push back:** request
  - an ASIC company extract and share-history search,
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company (relevant to Riverlark),
  - the share issue and transfer history with stamped and executed transfers,
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreements, including pre-emption and drag/tag rights,
  - Seller board approvals and authority for the sale,
  - Completion deliverables of executed transfers, original or replacement certificates, and releases of any share security.

### 16. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The DL says the lease requires notification only, and that the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. The playbook has no specific position on either, and nothing in the material shows a consent issue. **I would not escalate these on current information.**
- **Action:** confirm by reviewing the clauses ourselves, for example to check whether either contract contains a change-of-control definition that deems a share sale to be an assignment. Add a covenant that the lease notification is given in time.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "Reviewer Efficiency Note" / [STANDARD] labels | Clauses "cleared," framework "accepted" | **Reject in writing.** Nothing is agreed. All items are open. |
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m.** No fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority. |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar.** |
| 3 | Time limit and sweep-up | 18 months; limits apply to all Claims | **24 months.** Delete the sweep-up. Keep categories separate. |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge.** |
| 5 | Fraud | Limitations and non-reliance apply to all Claims | **Full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out. Non-negotiable.** |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus public records | **Specific fair disclosure only.** Delete DL 1.1–1.2. |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, including "discoverable" | **Delete.** Seller knowledge to be named persons with reasonable enquiry. |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | **CP: effective consent plus evidence that 11.3 conditions are met, before Completion.** |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion.** |
| 10 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **AUD 420k plus on-costs as a line item, or Seller-funded and indemnified.** |
| 11 | Ironquay | Payment-only indemnity | **Broaden to IP title/use loss. Preserve the SOW3 cure with verified payment and assignment.** |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preservation, investigation, updates and consultation covenants. No assumptions either way. Seek a specific indemnity.** |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Request information. Reserve treatment. No automatic deduction.** |
| 14 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **Open.** Separate categories. |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence: ASIC, PPSR, transfer history, authority.** |
| 16 | Lease/Mossvale | Notification / no consent | **Verify the clauses. Low priority on current facts.** |

**Process points:**
1. Send a short holding response rejecting the "agreed/cleared" framing before any substantive mark-up, so that silence cannot be read as acceptance.
2. Do not raise any playbook fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft.
3. Ask for a bring-down of all disclosed facts to a current date. The disclosures are as at 22 September 2026.
4. Use the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (paras 2, 3, 5, 6 and 10) to rebut its Update. On those points the Seller's specific disclosures support our position.

Also carve Fundamental, Tax, IP and specific-indemnity claims out of the general limitations.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2): whole-data-room and public-register disclosure
- **Playbook:** require specific fair disclosure. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- DL 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room. DL 1.2 adds the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." Taken together, nearly any warranty could be neutralised by something buried in the data room.
- DL 1.4 (no admission of breach, liability or requirement) is broadly acceptable in principle. However, it must not dilute the effect of specific disclosures against the warranties.
- **Push back:** delete DL 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should be limited to matters fairly disclosed in the specific paragraphs of the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter, and cross-referenced to the relevant warranty. The Seller has represented that the general disclosure is "without limiting any specific disclosure," so it cannot say the specific disclosures are inadequate.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): blanket exclusion, including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- This clause is worse than an actual-knowledge bar. It imputes constructive knowledge to us and our advisers, which would make our own due diligence a defence for the Seller. It would also defeat the specific indemnities, which exist precisely because we know about the issues.
- **Push back:** delete cl 8.3. Separately, make any Seller "awareness" qualifiers on warranties refer to named individuals' actual knowledge after reasonable enquiry. Those individuals should be identified from the Seller's management; the playbook does not name them, so we should propose names.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller says:** "addressed," with reasonable endeavours and consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the written consent.
- **The Seller's own DL para 2 says:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m). Clause 11.2 requires change-of-control consent, and clause 11.3 attaches conditions. **No final consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied has been provided.** The matter is therefore not "addressed."
- **Playbook:** effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied, before Completion. Consent-on-delivery is not enough. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.
- Under consent-on-delivery, a conditional consent whose 11.3 conditions are unmet could satisfy the Condition. We could then complete and lose 30% of revenue.
- **Push back:** a Condition Precedent requiring an unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, in form and substance satisfactory to the Buyer, plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met, delivered before Completion. Pair this with a stronger Seller obligation, such as all reasonable endeavours plus specified steps, and a Buyer-only right to waive.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller says:** release "to be provided following Completion."
- **DL para 3:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding. Change-of-control at 8.1, discharge at 9.2. **Not repaid, and no discharge provided.**
- **Playbook:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable lender undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval.
- On a debt-free basis, a post-Completion release leaves us acquiring a company with live security and a possible change-of-control default under 8.1. We would be relying on the Seller's goodwill to clear it.
- **Push back:** a Completion deliverable of a Riverlark payout letter dated close to Completion, payment directly from the funds flow, and executed releases and discharges (including PPSR) delivered at Completion. The amount must be deducted as Debt. We should not discuss any post-Completion route without Amelia's approval and a lender's irrevocable undertaking.

### 10. Employee bonuses (funds flow / DD-005)
- **Seller says:** the AUD 420k bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. **DL para 5 confirms** they are absent from the funds flow and does not address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or be seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- The bonuses are Company liabilities triggered by Completion. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company, and therefore we, would bear them, plus on-costs.
- **Push back:** either deduct them as Debt or a transaction cost, with on-costs, as an express line item paid through payroll at Completion, or obtain a Seller-funded mechanism backed by a specific indemnity covering the amounts and all on-costs. The on-cost amount must be quantified; it has not been.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Seller says:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate."
- **DL para 4:** transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, which is unverified. There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- A payment-only indemnity does not address the real risk, which is that the Company does not own IP it uses. That exposes us to infringement claims, loss of use, re-development cost and third-party claims, none of which are capped at the outstanding fee.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to or right to use the Ironquay deliverables, including infringement claims.
  - Keep the cure route: payment of outstanding SOW3 fees at or before Completion, verified by a bank/remittance record and Ironquay's written confirmation, plus a confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable.
  - Exclude the indemnity from the general limitations.
  - Do not treat AUD 180k as the confirmed figure in either direction.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6, DD-006)
- **Seller says:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **DL para 6:** a download link was sent to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records may be affected (names, business emails, roles, timestamps). Access, scope and notification obligation are not established, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- We should not accept the Seller's "not expected to be material" characterisation, because the investigation has not concluded. We also should not overstate the matter or assert a notifiable breach or a loss figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete a proper investigation (independent if appropriate), give regular written updates and the final findings to the Buyer, and consult the Buyer before any notification or regulator/customer communication.
  - Strike "not expected to be material" from any warranty or disclosure language.
  - Seek a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, outside the general limitations.
  - Request a current status update, since the latest disclosure is from 22 September.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011, AUD 330k)
- **Seller says:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **DL para 8:** three related renewals of AUD 110k each, to be read together for timing and scope. The DL does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** assess them, with no automatic Debt classification and no price deduction.
- The Seller has asserted "ordinary course" without support, and its own disclosure does not establish it. We should not concede the characterisation, but our playbook does not support demanding a deduction either.
- **Action:** request the contracts, timing, termination rights, accrual status and business rationale. Ask whether the three renewals were split, related or accelerated before Completion. Reserve the position on treatment, such as Debt, working capital, indemnity or an ordinary-course covenant, until the facts are assessed.

### 14. Tax / IP warranties
- **Seller says:** "settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- They are not settled. Placing them in the general regime with a 20% cap and 18 months would be the hidden override flagged in item 3.
- **Response:** state that Tax and IP remain open and are to be negotiated as separate categories. Do not assert unlimited liability as a position either.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
- **Seller says:** title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. **DL para 10** itself acknowledges that this is only the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Playbook:** require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Push back:** request
  - an ASIC company extract and share-history search,
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company (relevant to Riverlark),
  - the share issue and transfer history with stamped and executed transfers,
  - the constitution and any shareholder agreements, including pre-emption and drag/tag rights,
  - Seller board approvals and authority for the sale,
  - Completion deliverables of executed transfers, original or replacement certificates, and releases of any share security.

### 16. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The DL says the lease requires notification only, and that the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. The playbook has no specific position on either, and nothing in the material shows a consent issue. **I would not escalate these on current information.**
- **Action:** confirm by reviewing the clauses ourselves, for example to check whether either contract contains a change-of-control definition that deems a share sale to be an assignment. Add a covenant that the lease notification is given in time.
